::: {#rem-shannon-vs-hamming}
#### Random errors and worst-case errors

[Source coding](source-coding.qmd) removes redundancy from a message;
error-correcting codes add redundancy back, in a controlled way,
so that the receiver can undo changes to the message.
@shannon1948mathematical modeled those changes by chance
and found that a code can make
the [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) of a decoding mistake as small as wanted
at every [rate](#def-code-rate) below the
[channel capacity](channel-capacity.qmd#def-channel-capacity),
and at no rate above it.
The codes on this page instead guard against any pattern of
up to $t$ changed symbols, however they arise,
which is the model complexity theory uses.

:::
